name: Electric piano
credit: jRhodes3 — a 1977 Rhodes Mark I Stage 73 sampled by Jeff Learman
_what: The mono set, not the stereo one: a melodic bank is mono by contract,
and jRhodes3c's stereo files are the mono ones with a mid-side
pitch-shift doubling on them that cancels when they are summed. Folding
those would spend the decode on an effect that then deletes itself.
Sampled every fourth white key, which is a five- or six-semitone grid,
so this recipe keeps every note the source has across the keys range
_notes: Every pitch the library samples from A2 up to D6: the grid is the
player's, not ours. A2 and D6 are outside the 48-84 the keys line uses
and are in the bank anyway, because without them C3 and C6 would be
built from a sample three semitones away when one two semitones away
exists. Worst stretch across the range: three semitones, at the one
six-semitone gap the source leaves between F4 and B4.
_layers: The source has five velocity layers and the bank keeps three. Not a
size decision — five would be 11.7 MB and the ceiling is 12: it is that
`voices::MAX_LAYERS` is four and `jam::voice_layer` only ever asks for
one, two or three. Layers four and five would be files the engine
cannot index. The three kept are the softest, the middle and the
hardest of the five velocity bands.
`layer_by` is `dynamic` here and `loudness` on the basses, and the
reason is in pick_layers_by_dynamic: this set's five layers are
recorded at one peak within 1.9 dB, with the softest measuring LOUDER
than the hardest, because an SFZ player supplies the level from
velocity. Measured for loudness the ladder comes out as three
neighbours in the wrong order; ordered by velocity band it is the soft,
middle and barking Rhodes the player recorded.
_cap: 2.5 s, and this is the voice the cap costs most. jRhodes3c is a LOOPED
set — the samples are a few seconds long and sustain on a loop point
rather than decaying — so every note here runs to the cap and lands on
the 30 ms fade instead of ringing out the way a Rhodes does under a
held chord. A comping voice plays chords shorter than that, so it is
the right trade, but it is a trade.
_release: The source's own `ampeg_release=0.300`, clamped to the 250 ms
`voices::MAX_RELEASE_MS` allows. A tine under a damper is the longest
release of any voice here and it still wants more than the format gives
